title: Which Training Intensity Distribution Intervention will Produce the Greatest Improvements in Maximal Oxygen Uptake and Time-Trial Performance in Endurance Athletes? A Systematic Review and Network Meta-analysis of Individual Participant Data
authors: Rosenblat MA, Watt JA, Arnold JI, Treff G, Sandbakk OB, Esteve-Lanao J, et al.
population: Recreational (n=150) and competitive (n=198) endurance athletes; 13 studies; mean age 17.6-41.5 y; VO2max 46.6-68.3 mL/kg/min; 52 female
findings: 13 studies, 348 athletes (296 male, 52 female); Medline and SPORTDiscus searched to 11 February 2024.
Using time-in-HR-zone: no difference between polarized and pyramidal for VO2max (SMD -0.06, p=0.68) or time trial (SMD -0.05, p=0.34); no significant difference between polarized and any other TID.
Subgroup analysis: significant difference in VO2max response between recreational and competitive athletes for polarized vs pyramidal (SMD -0.63).
Authors conclude competitive athletes may benefit from polarized and recreational athletes from pyramidal TID.
limitations: Only 13 studies with short interventions; 15% female; VO2max and time trial are surrogates; subgroup finding is exploratory (the p-value for it is truncated in the Europe PMC and PubMed abstract text, which states only that it was statistically significant).
implications: For recreational runners default to pyramidal (zone 1 dominant, zone 2 > zone 3, both small); allow polarized only for competitive athletes with demonstrated training age.
Treat polarized and pyramidal as equivalent for time-trial performance; choose by phase, race distance and tolerance rather than claimed superiority.
Make TID type a function of athlete level in the generator's input model.

verification.notes: Crossref: online 2025-01-31, print Mar 2025. Researcher quoted 'p<0.05' for the subgroup; abstract text is cut off at that point, so p-value removed. Counts and SMDs verified.
